messages:
From: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@heliosoft.com>
To: priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 14:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Dedicated sizing inputs for HelioSoft pilot

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the quick chat this morning. As discussed, HelioSoft is preparing an internal business case for a dedicated GPU pool to run our retrieval-augmented generation and embeddings pipelines for customer support. We want to get a sizing estimate from Redwood so we can budget for Q3.

High-level asks:
- An initial dedicated capacity sizing (GPU SKUs / slot counts / expected sustained throughput) based on our traffic.
- Notes on latency SLOs we can meet at different commit levels.
- Any immediate recommendations that would materially change unit cost (quantization, session affinity, batching).

I don’t yet have a formatted traffic file — I can provide a short CSV with sample peak hour API calls, average prompt length and average model response length. Could you send whatever pre-sales questionnaire / spreadsheet you prefer we fill?

Goal: get a back-of-envelope sizing by next week and a 30–45 minute sizing call the week after. Procurement (procurement@heliosoft.com) is looped for timing and contract questions.

Thanks,
Alex Jenkins
Head of Platform
HelioSoft

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@heliosoft.com>
Cc: procurement@heliosoft.com
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing inputs for HelioSoft pilot

Thanks Alex — great to connect.

Attaching our dedicated preflight worksheet (redwood_dedicated_preflight_v2.xlsx). If you can fill the yellow fields we’ll be able to produce a first-pass sizing and a recommended commit/slots map. Key fields we need filled:

- Peak concurrent sessions (p95 peak window, sessions/minute)
- Average prompt token length (median + 90th pct)
- Average response token length (median + 90th pct)
- % of calls that are chat (multi-turn) vs stateless generation
- Expected peak queries per second (qps) and sustained qps in business hours
- Latency SLO target (p95 end-to-end generation latency)
- Any regulatory constraints (VPC, audit logs, retention)

If you can send a small sample telemetry CSV (3–7 days) with timestamped requests and token counts that’s even better — we can run the worksheet through our capacity model and return an estimated GPU SKU mix and expected per-token cost.

I’ll also propose a short internal review with our sizing team to lock assumptions before the customer call; copying procurement for potential timeline constraints. Proposed windows for the call: 2027-04-28 or 2027-04-29 afternoon PT. Which works?

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_preflight_v2.xlsx (worksheet), sample_instructions.txt

Best,
Priyom Das
Solutions Architect, Pre-sales
Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated sizing inputs for HelioSoft pilot — draft assumptions

Marissa / Ben — forwarding the Helio thread. Alex says they will deliver a short CSV but wants a back-of-envelope ASAP. I put together quick assumptions below to get us started; can you review and correct where needed? I plan to send the filled worksheet back Thursday next week unless you ask for an earlier turnaround.

My initial read / suggested defaults for an enterprise-support RAG workload:
- Model family: 13B-33B class baseline (they mentioned embeddings + RAG) -> assume a 33B-ish model for latency SLOs unless they say otherwise.
- Target p95 latency: 800ms end-to-end for single-turn prompts, 1.2s for RAG+LLM (retrieval + decoding).
- Prompt/response tokens: use median prompt 40 tokens, median response 120 tokens; 90th pct prompt 150 / response 512.
- Peak concurrent sessions (p95 peak window): estimate 350 concurrent sessions -> assume 20% peak burst factor (=> 420 transient).
- Average session length / multi-turn: 1.8 turns per session; 65% stateless, 35% multi-turn.
- Traffic profile: peak qps of ~70 sustained for 10–20 minutes, average qps outside peak ~12.

From that, rough GPU assignment options:
- Conservative commit (higher SLO, higher cost): 8x A100-80GB equiv (slot-based mapping), oversubscription 1.1
- Balanced commit (recommended starting): 4–6x H100-80GB equiv with session-slotting and KV cache enabled, conservative batching -> expected p95 under 1s for single-turn
- Aggressive cost-optimized: 3–4x L4/RTX-class quantized variants with heavy batching and more burst fallback; higher tail latency risk.

Questions for you:
1) Should we assume they will use half as many embeddings queries vs generation queries? (they cited embeddings but not mix)
2) For costing, do we include a 10% buffer for autoscale and headroom? I usually bake in 15% but can relax.

I have a slot-based model workbook that maps token/sec -> slots -> GPU SKUs; I’ll attach a draft sizing estimate once you confirm the assumptions.

— Priyom

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated sizing inputs for HelioSoft pilot — draft assumptions

Thanks — these assumptions look reasonable as a starting point. A few suggested edits before we send to the customer:

- Lower median response to 100 tokens (they're a support use case, shorter answers expected) and keep 90th at 512 for edge cases.
- Set peak concurrent sessions to 300 (their traffic profile sounded a bit lighter) with a 25% burst allowance.
- Recommend H100-80GB mix for baseline; propose a canary node with a quantized 33B variant to validate cost/perf tradeoffs.
- For autoscale buffer, use 12% for the initial proposal (we can flag as negotiable).

I attached a quick sizing_estimate_helio_v1.xlsx with the slot mapping for the balanced commit option — numbers are rough but will give procurement something to kick off budgeting.

Minor editorial: change the wording in the spreadsheet notes from "sessions" to "active sessions (connected sockets)" — a better reflection of their architecture.

If you want, I can take this to a 15-minute sync on Tuesday to finalize before we send.

— Marissa

Attachment: sizing_estimate_helio_v1.xlsx

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: HelioSoft dedicated sizing — initial worksheet and proposed meeting

Alex — thanks for sending the CSV (attached as helio_preflight_inputs.csv). We filled the worksheet and produced an initial sizing estimate (attached: redwood_dedicated_preflight_v2_filled.xlsx and sizing_estimate_helio_v1.xlsx). High-level summary:

- Recommended starting commit: Balanced tier using 5x H100-80GB equivalent slots (session-slotting + KV cache) with a 12% autoscale buffer.
- Expected sustained qps during peak: ~65–75 with p95 single-turn latency ~850ms.
- Cost notes: using a quantized fallback for non-critical batch workloads reduces effective per-token cost by ~22% on our simulation; we recommend a canary quantized node for 2 weeks to validate quality.

Next step: propose a 30–45 minute sizing review to walk the worksheet and confirm model family and latency targets. My calendar link: https://calendar.redwoodinference.com/meet/rdw-helio-sizing-20270429 — I’m proposing 2027-04-29 15:00 PT; please suggest an alternate if that doesn’t work.

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_preflight_v2_filled.xlsx, sizing_estimate_helio_v1.xlsx, helio_preflight_inputs.csv

Thanks and looking forward,
Priyom Das
Solutions Architect, Pre-sales
Redwood Inference
